import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.52

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy problem?

The notebook adds the remark that there is an algorithm to decide conjugacy to a given
(fixed) element of the group.

Here "rank" is the Prüfer rank (Mal'cev special rank): a group has finite rank if there is
$r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by at most
$r$ elements. A finitely presented group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ has
soluble conjugacy problem if there is an algorithm which decides, for any two words $u, v$
in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$, whether $u$ and $v$ represent conjugate elements of the group.
Whether the conjugacy problem is soluble does not depend on the finite presentation chosen.

Every finitely presented group is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for some `n : ℕ` and
some finite set `rels` of relators in the free group on `Fin n`, so the question is
formalised by quantifying over such presentations.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.52»

/-- A group $G$ has finite (Prüfer) rank if there is $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every
finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements. -/
def HasFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

/-- The finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$ has soluble
conjugacy problem if the set of pairs of words $(u, v)$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ such that
$u$ and $v$ represent conjugate elements of the presented group is decidable. Words are
modelled as lists of pairs `(i, b)`, where `b = true` stands for $x_i$ and `b = false` for
$x_i^{-1}$. -/
def HasSolvableConjugacyProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) =>
    IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.1)) (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.2))

/--
Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy problem?

Every finitely presented group is isomorphic to $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$
with $R$ finite, so the question is stated for all such presentations.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.52» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) →
      HasFiniteRank (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) →
      HasSolvableConjugacyProblem (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) := by
  sorry

/-- A finite group has finite rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem HasFiniteRank.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : HasFiniteRank G := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have := Fintype.ofFinite G
  calc Group.rank H ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset H).card := Group.rank_le (by simp)
    _ = Nat.card H := by simp [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
    _ ≤ Nat.card G := Subgroup.card_le_card_group H

/-- The trivial group has finite rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem HasFiniteRank.of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : HasFiniteRank G :=
  HasFiniteRank.of_finite G

/-- The trivial presentation (no generators, no relators) has soluble conjugacy problem. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem HasSolvableConjugacyProblem.zero :
    HasSolvableConjugacyProblem (∅ : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))) := by
  have h (p : List (Fin 0 × Bool) × List (Fin 0 × Bool)) :
      IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk ∅ (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
        (PresentedGroup.mk ∅ (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
    rw [Subsingleton.elim (FreeGroup.mk p.1) (FreeGroup.mk p.2)]
  letI : DecidablePred fun p : List (Fin 0 × Bool) × List (Fin 0 × Bool) =>
      IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk ∅ (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
        (PresentedGroup.mk ∅ (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) :=
    fun p => isTrue (h p)
  exact Computable.computablePred <|
    (Computable.const true).of_eq fun p => (decide_eq_true (h p)).symm

end Kourovka.«9.52»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition (one yes/no question, the Note carrying no separate question) matches the statement.
modeling_decisions: Finitely presented groups are represented directly as `PresentedGroup ↑rels` with generator type `Fin n` and `rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))`, quantifying over all such presentations rather than over abstract groups `G` with an isomorphism to a presented group. Every finitely presented group is isomorphic to one of these and `IsSolvable`/`HasFiniteRank` are isomorphism-invariant, so this is equivalent.

'Finite rank' is read as finite Prüfer (Mal'cev special) rank: `∃ r, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r`, following the decomposition note and Robinson's usage. For finitely generated soluble groups this coincides with finite abelian section rank / being minimax, so the standard alternative readings agree here (but not with torsion-free rank, which is not the intended notion).

'Soluble conjugacy problem' is formalised as the uniform conjugacy problem for the given finite presentation: `ComputablePred` (Mathlib, via `Primcodable` encodings of `List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool)`) of the predicate 'the two words represent conjugate elements' (`IsConj`). Words are lists of (generator, Bool) letters mapped through `FreeGroup.mk` and `PresentedGroup.mk`. Since decidability of the conjugacy problem is independent of the finite presentation, requiring it for every presentation of the group (which the ∀ over `n, rels` does) is equivalent to requiring it for one.
The trailing 'Note' sentence (conjugacy to a fixed element is decidable) is recorded in the module docstring only, as the decomposition table specifies it poses no separate question.

AMS tags `3 20` (mathematical logic/computability and group theory). Three `@[category test]` lemmas with short proofs were added as basic API for the bespoke definitions (finite groups have finite rank; the trivial group has finite rank; the empty presentation on `Fin 0` has soluble conjugacy problem).

/-!
# Conjecture 9.52

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy problem?
Here finite rank means finite Prüfer rank, and a soluble conjugacy problem means that, for a fixed
finite presentation, there is an algorithm deciding whether any two input words are conjugate.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.52»

/-- A word in the free group on `n` generators. The Boolean records whether a letter is inverted. -/
abbrev Word (n : ℕ) := List (Fin n × Bool)

/-- A group has finite Prüfer rank if there is a uniform finite bound on the number of generators
needed for each of its finitely generated subgroups. -/
def HasFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ S : Finset G, ∃ T : Finset G,
    T.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (T : Set G) = Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)

/-- The uniform conjugacy problem for a fixed finite presentation is soluble if conjugacy of any
pair of input words is a computable predicate. -/
def HasSolubleConjugacyProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Finset (Word n)) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun words : Word n × Word n =>
    IsConj
      (PresentedGroup.mk (FreeGroup.mk '' (rels : Set (Word n))) (FreeGroup.mk words.1))
      (PresentedGroup.mk (FreeGroup.mk '' (rels : Set (Word n))) (FreeGroup.mk words.2))

/--
Does every finitely presented soluble group of finite Prüfer rank have soluble uniform conjugacy
problem? Equivalently, for every finite presentation of such a group, is there an algorithm which,
given two words in its generators, decides whether the represented group elements are conjugate?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.52» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (Word n)),
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (FreeGroup.mk '' (rels : Set (Word n)))) →
      HasFiniteRank (PresentedGroup (FreeGroup.mk '' (rels : Set (Word n)))) →
      HasSolubleConjugacyProblem rels := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.52»
modeling_decisions: A finitely presented group is quantified via all explicit finite presentations: `n` generators and a `Finset` of relator words. The associated group is Mathlib's `PresentedGroup`.
Finite rank is interpreted as finite Prüfer rank: one natural number uniformly bounds the size of a generating set for every finitely generated subgroup.
The uniform conjugacy problem is stated on pairs of raw words in the fixed presentation. Their images under the presentation quotient are tested with Mathlib's `IsConj`.
Algorithmic decidability is represented by Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, not plain `DecidableRel`, which would admit non-effective classical instances.
The trailing note about deciding conjugacy to a single fixed element is contextual information and is not stated as a separate theorem, in accordance with the decomposition table.

The rank here is the Prüfer (or Mal'cev) rank: there is a uniform finite bound on the number of
generators needed by any finitely generated subgroup. The conjugacy problem asks for one algorithm

namespace Kourovka.«9.52»

/-- A group has finite Prüfer rank if the numbers of generators needed by its finitely generated
subgroups have a common finite bound. -/
def HasFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = H

/-- The uniform conjugacy problem for a finite presentation is soluble if a computable Boolean
function decides, for every pair of words, whether their images in the presented group are
conjugate. -/
def HasSolubleConjugacyProblem {n m : ℕ} (rels : Fin m → FreeGroup (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ algorithm : List (Fin n × Bool) → List (Fin n × Bool) → Bool,
    Computable₂ algorithm ∧
      ∀ u v, algorithm u v = true ↔
        IsConj
          (PresentedGroup.mk (Set.range rels) (FreeGroup.mk u))
          (PresentedGroup.mk (Set.range rels) (FreeGroup.mk v))

/--
Does every finitely presented soluble group of finite Prüfer (Mal'cev) rank have a soluble uniform
conjugacy problem? Equivalently, for every finite presentation of such a group, is there an
algorithm deciding for every pair of words whether they represent conjugate elements? The notebook
notes that conjugacy to any one fixed element can already be decided.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.52» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (rels : Fin m → FreeGroup (Fin n)),
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (Set.range rels)) →
      HasFiniteRank (PresentedGroup (Set.range rels)) →
      HasSolubleConjugacyProblem rels := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.52»
modeling_decisions: Finite presentations are represented by natural numbers n and m and a relator enumeration `Fin m → FreeGroup (Fin n)`; the corresponding group is `PresentedGroup (Set.range rels)`.

Finite Prüfer/Mal'cev rank is expressed by the existence of one natural-number bound such that every finitely generated subgroup has an ambient finite generating set of cardinality at most that bound.

The uniform conjugacy algorithm takes two literal words `List (Fin n × Bool)`, not quotient-valued free-group elements, and is required to be a total `Computable₂` Boolean function that exactly classifies conjugacy of their images in the presented group.
The source's trailing note is retained in the theorem docstring but creates no additional declaration, in accordance with the decomposition table.

# Conjecture 9.52

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy
problem? Here finite rank means finite Prüfer rank, and soluble conjugacy
problem means that the uniform conjugacy problem for a fixed finite
presentation is decidable.

The source also notes that there is an algorithm to decide conjugacy to any

namespace Kourovka.«9.52»

/-- A word in `n` generators. A letter `(i, false)` denotes the generator `i`,
and `(i, true)` denotes its inverse. -/
abbrev Word (n : ℕ) := List (Fin n × Bool)

/-- The element of the free group represented by a signed word. -/
def wordValue {n : ℕ} : Word n → FreeGroup (Fin n)
  | [] => 1
  | (i, false) :: w => FreeGroup.of i * wordValue w
  | (i, true) :: w => (FreeGroup.of i)⁻¹ * wordValue w

/-- A group has finite Prüfer rank if the numbers of generators needed by its
finitely generated subgroups have a uniform finite bound. -/
def IsFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ S : Finset H, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set H) = ⊤

/-- The finite presentation with `n` generators and relator words `R`. -/
abbrev PresentedBy {n : ℕ} (R : Finset (Word n)) :=
  PresentedGroup (wordValue '' (R : Set (Word n)))

/-- The uniform conjugacy problem for a fixed finite presentation is soluble
if a total computable Boolean function decides, for every pair of words,
whether the represented elements are conjugate. -/
def HasSolubleConjugacyProblem {n : ℕ} (R : Finset (Word n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ decideConjugacy : Word n → Word n → Bool,
    Computable₂ decideConjugacy ∧
      ∀ u v : Word n,
        decideConjugacy u v = true ↔
          IsConj
            (PresentedGroup.mk _ (wordValue u) : PresentedBy R)
            (PresentedGroup.mk _ (wordValue v) : PresentedBy R)

/--
Does every finitely presented soluble group of finite Prüfer rank have soluble
uniform conjugacy problem? Equivalently, for every finite presentation whose
presented group is soluble and has finite Prüfer rank, is conjugacy of pairs of
words decidable by one algorithm?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.52» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (R : Finset (Word n)),
      IsSolvable (PresentedBy R) → IsFiniteRank (PresentedBy R) →
        HasSolubleConjugacyProblem R := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.52»
modeling_decisions: A finite presentation is encoded by a natural number n of generators and a finite set of signed-generator words; its group is Mathlib's PresentedGroup of the evaluated relators.
Finite rank is interpreted as finite Prüfer rank: there is one natural-number bound on the size of a generating set for every finitely generated subgroup.
Solubility is represented by Mathlib's IsSolvable predicate.
A soluble uniform conjugacy problem for a fixed presentation means the existence of one total Computable₂ Boolean function on two words whose true outputs are exactly the conjugate pairs.
The notebook's trailing note about conjugacy to one fixed element is documented but is not made a separate declaration, as required by the decomposition.

modeling_decisions: A finite presentation is represented by a natural number n of generators and a Finset of raw words List (Fin n × Bool); the relators are their images under FreeGroup.mk, and PresentedGroup forms the quotient by their normal closure.
Finite Prüfer/Mal'cev rank is modeled as the existence of a uniform natural bound r such that every finitely generated subgroup has a generating Finset of cardinality at most r.

A soluble conjugacy problem for a fixed presentation is modeled by ComputablePred on pairs of raw input words, asserting that their images in the presented group are IsConj. The algorithm may depend on the fixed presentation, as required.
